streets.length: about 1 km in OSM (13 ways); the historic-centre stretch runs from Calea Victoriei to Calea Moșilor
history_and_buildings: Named after the "lipscani", merchants selling goods brought from Leipzig (Lipsca); a lane since the early 18th century.

Eclectic late-19th/early-20th-c. fronts (Renaissance, baroque, rococo and neoclassical elements). Nationalised 1948, badly degraded after the 1980s; restored and repaved in the early 2010s, when ruins of medieval inns were found under the paving.

Notable fronts: Banca Berliner Gesellschaft (1910–13); Hanul Gabroveni (1739, rebuilt, entrance from Lipscani); Hanul cu Tei (1833, a passage to Blănari); Cărturești Carusel at no. 55 (an 1860s bank building, bookshop since 2015); the National Bank (BNR) old palace on the S side between Smârdan and Doamnei.
Today a pedestrian street of bars, restaurants and some chain shops.

venues_osm.name: Parchetul de pe lângă Judecătoria Sector 4 și Sector 1

streets.length: 220 m (ro.wikipedia) / 231 m OSM, from Șelari to Bd. I.C. Brătianu with a slight right-hand bend; Strada Zarafi to Lipscani at about 110 m, Pasajul Francez to Covaci 40 m further on
history_and_buildings: Named after Gabrovo (Bulgaria) knife merchants.
I.L. Caragiale opened the "Berăria Mihalcea și Caragiale" here in 1893.
Mostly late-19th/early-20th-c. buildings; the whole street is a listed architectural ensemble (LMI B-II-a-B-18798). After rehabilitation: shops, pubs, fast food and pizzerias.

streets.length: 260 m, north–south from Lipscani to Splaiul Independenței
history_and_buildings: Named after the saddlers (șelari) who had their workshops here.
House at nos. 20–22 (late 19th c.) is a listed monument, B-II-m-B-19749.

streets.length: 210 m (ro.wikipedia) / 320 m OSM incl. continuation, west–east from Șelari to Sfântul Anton; Strada Soarelui to the back of Curtea Veche at about 60 m
history_and_buildings: From Old Slavonic kovačĭ, "smith".
Venues of tradition: Cafeneaua Veche ("the oldest attested café in Bucharest") and Taverna Covaci, next to where mici (mititei) were invented.
Laid out in the early 19th c. ("Strada Nouă"); called Covaci since 1852. Setting of the tavern in Mateiu Caragiale's "Craii de Curtea-Veche" (1910). OSM surface: setts (cobbles).

streets.length: 370 m arc, north to south from Strada Doamnei to Șelari, crossing Lipscani and Stavropoleos about halfway
history_and_buildings: One of the first Old Town streets renovated and repaved. Formerly Ulița Nemților / German Street, first documented 1 May 1672; named Smârdan since 1878 after the 1877 battle.
19th c.: shops, workshops and hotels such as Hotel Brenner / Hotel d'Europe.
At no. 39 (former Hotel Concordia), on 23 January 1859, the National Party decided to elect the same prince (Cuza) for Moldavia and Wallachia.
Former Banca Agricolă building; a house now Van Gogh Café; the old National Bank wing.

streets.length: 526 m OSM, from the Piața Unirii side to Calea Victoriei; probably the oldest street keeping its medieval line
history_and_buildings: Lined mostly with 19th-c. houses: the great fire of 1847 started here.
Listed ensemble B-II-a-B-18765.
Curtea Veche church ensemble at no. 33 (Buna Vestire church 1559, parish house).
Hanul lui Manuc at no. 62.

hanul-cu-tei.name: Hanul cu Tei
hanul-cu-tei.facts: Built 1833 by Anastasie Hagi Gheorghe Polizu and Ștefan Popovici. The only Bucharest inn kept in its original form. A 75 m north–south passage between Lipscani and Blănari: shops over vaulted cellars (14 per owner) and richly ornamented iron gates at both ends. The owners' monogram "A.P." and "S.P." is visible at the Blănari entrance, and "1833" is carved over the entrance. Today art galleries, plus a bar in the cellar.

hanul-lui-manuc.name: Hanul lui Manuc
hanul-lui-manuc.facts: Built 1806–1808 by Manuc Bei; the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest was signed here. Four large wings joined by two tiers of wooden galleries (arcaded ground floor, wooden gallery with balustrades above) around a courtyard. A grand staircase sits under a kiosk with a pointed roof and projecting rafters. Historically 15 vaulted cellars, 23 shops on the ground floor and 107 rooms upstairs. Restored by the Cantacuzino heirs (2012). Today restaurants, cafés and a courtyard terrace; Franceză 62 (LMI B-II-m-A-18788).

curtea-veche.name: Curtea Veche
curtea-veche.facts: The first princely court of Bucharest (probably from Mircea cel Bătrân, late 14th/early 15th c.). Vlad III dated a document from his "fortress of Bucharest" here on 20 September 1459. Unused after the 1718 fire and 1738 earthquake. The ruins of the voivodal palace are now a protected archaeological site and the Curtea Veche Museum. The Buna Vestire church (1559) is the oldest church in Bucharest kept in its original form. The court spread between Halelor, Șelari, Lipscani, Bărăției and Calea Moșilor.
